We need to determine if the response conflicts with available context, tool evidence, tool contract, or explicit governing instruction.

We have the conversation: user wants to check balance of gold rewards card. Agent asked for identity verification. User gave name and email. Agent called get_user_information_by_email -> no records. Then get_user_information_by_name -> found record with email kenji.tanaka@outlook.com, phone 206-555-0293, address, DOB. Then agent asked user to confirm any two of: DOB, phone, address, email (the one linked to account). User said they entered wrong email, meant the one found, phone number is 206-555-0293, unfortunately DOB and address not at hand. So user provided phone number (matches) and implicitly email? They said they meant the one found (kenji.tanaka@outlook.com). They didn't explicitly state email but said they meant that. They gave phone number. They didn't give DOB or address. So they have provided phone number and implicitly email (they said they meant that). However, they didn't explicitly state email; but they said "Я имел в виду тот, который вы нашли." That refers to the email found. So they are confirming email matches. So they have provided phone and email (implicitly). That's two pieces: phone number and email. According to policy, need to verify identity by ensuring they can give correctly any 2 out of the following values: date of birth, email, phone number, address. They gave phone number and email (implicitly). That should be sufficient.
